Job Description

Associate Director, Clinical Operations - Country Operations Lead– FSP


Role Purpose

The Associate Director, Clinical Operations – FSP provides operational leadership for Clinical Operations within an assigned client-aligned portfolio. The role is accountable for ensuring effective operational execution of clinical deliverables, with a strong focus on client expectations, project delivery, quality, performance and proactive risk management.

Working closely with client stakeholders, Project Delivery and functional leadership, the Associate Director translates client and portfolio priorities into clear operational plans and ensures Clinical Operations teams are positioned to deliver against current and future project requirements.

The role requires a strong FSP and client-focused mindset, combining operational leadership with strategic thinking, proactive planning and effective people leadership. The Associate Director is expected to anticipate challenges, identify opportunities to improve delivery and ensure teams remain closely connected to client priorities and project outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Client-Aligned Operational & Delivery Leadership

  • Provide operational leadership across the assigned client-aligned portfolio, ensuring Clinical Operations activities support client priorities, project objectives and delivery commitments.
  • Develop a strong understanding of the client's portfolio, strategy, expectations and ways of working and translate these into clear operational priorities for Clinical Operations teams.
  • Partner closely with client stakeholders, Project Delivery and functional leadership to ensure alignment between client expectations and operational execution.
  • Maintain oversight of clinical delivery performance across the portfolio, including study start-up, monitoring, site management and other applicable clinical deliverables.
  • Develop and drive operational strategies that support successful project and portfolio delivery within agreed quality, timeline and financial expectations.
  • Take a forward-looking view of the portfolio, anticipating changes in client demand, project activity, operational complexity and capability requirements.
  • Proactively identify trends, dependencies, risks and potential barriers to delivery and ensure appropriate mitigation plans are established before they impact client outcomes.
  • Use operational data, project intelligence and leading indicators to inform priorities and support effective decision-making.
  • Ensure emerging delivery risks and potential solutions are communicated through appropriate client and internal governance and escalation pathways.
  • Identify recurring operational challenges and work across functions to address root causes and implement sustainable solutions.
  • Build strong, trusted relationships with client and internal stakeholders and provide clear, transparent communication regarding operational performance, risks and priorities.
  • Participate in client governance and operational meetings as appropriate, representing Clinical Operations and ensuring actions and commitments are effectively followed through.
  • Seek and respond to client feedback, identifying opportunities to continuously improve operational delivery and strengthen the client partnership.
  • Promote collaboration across Clinical Operations, Project Delivery and other functions to ensure an integrated approach to client delivery.
  • Balance immediate project needs with longer-term portfolio priorities, ensuring operational decisions support both current delivery and future client requirements.
  • Challenge existing approaches where appropriate and identify opportunities to improve quality, efficiency, consistency and the overall client experience.

People Leadership & Organizational Capability

  • Lead, coach and develop Clinical Operations managers and teams, establishing clear expectations for performance, accountability, quality and client delivery.
  • Create an environment in which managers and teams understand client priorities and how their work contributes to successful project and portfolio outcomes.
  • Promote a proactive rather than reactive culture, encouraging teams to anticipate risks, identify solutions and take ownership before issues require escalation.
  • Develop managers to make effective decisions, lead through complexity and operate successfully within a matrix and client-aligned environment.
  • Ensure appropriate performance management, development planning, succession planning and talent development across the assigned organization.
  • Identify current and future capability needs and ensure teams have the appropriate skills, experience and leadership capability to support the client portfolio.
  • Foster collaboration, knowledge sharing and consistency across teams and actively address siloed ways of working.
  • Create an environment where employees are encouraged to raise risks early, challenge constructively and contribute ideas to improve client delivery.

Resource & Capacity Management

  • Ensure appropriate resource capacity and capability are available to support client and project delivery requirements.
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of resource demand based on the client portfolio, project forecasts, timelines and anticipated changes in workload.
  • Partner with Project Delivery and functional leadership to align resource deployment with project priorities and delivery needs.
  • Identify potential capacity or capability gaps early and implement appropriate mitigation plans.
  • Support recruitment, deployment and talent decisions based on both current requirements and anticipated portfolio demand.
  • Monitor utilization, capacity and productivity and take appropriate action to maintain effective and sustainable delivery.

Quality, Risk & Operational Excellence

  • Ensure clinical deliverables are executed in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, client expectations, quality standards, policies and procedures.
  • Maintain oversight of key operational and quality indicators and ensure appropriate action is taken where performance is below expectation.
  • Promote early identification, communication and management of operational and quality risks.
  • Ensure appropriate corrective and preventive actions are implemented and monitored where required.
  • Drive continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to simplify processes, improve ways of working and strengthen delivery performance.
  • Support and participate in audits, inspections and quality initiatives as appropriate.
  • Contribute to regional, global and cross-functional initiatives and process improvement activities.

Financial & Business Management

  • Maintain appropriate oversight of financial performance associated with the assigned operational organization.
  • Manage budgeting and forecasting activities within the assigned scope.
  • Understand the financial implications of operational, resource and delivery decisions and incorporate these considerations into decision-making.
  • Partner with relevant stakeholders to identify and address financial risks associated with client and project delivery.
  • Support efficient use of resources while maintaining quality and delivery expectations.

Education and Experience Requirements:

• Bachelor's Degree in a life science related field.
• Significant clinical research experience (comparable to 10+ years) including remote and clinical monitoring and experience in all phases of study life cycle, including start up, interim and close out.
• Line management experience appropriate to the size and complexity of the clinical management group in the designated country/region.

• Proven leadership skills.

• Valid Driver's License.

• Valid Passport.
In some cases an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individua

Why Join Us?

When you join Thermo Fisher Scientific, you become part of a global team that values passion, innovation, and a commitment to scientific excellence. You’ll work in an environment where collaboration and development are part of the everyday experience—and where your contributions truly make a difference.

Apply today to help us deliver tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

Clarity Innovations is a trusted national security partner, dedicated to safeguarding our nation’s interests and delivering innovative solutions that empower the Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of Defense (DoD) to transform data into actionable intelligence, ensuring mission success in an evolving world.

Our mission-first software and data engineering platform modernizes data operations, utilizing advanced workflows, CI/CD, and secure DevSecOps practices. We focus on challenges in Information Warfare, Cyber Operations, Operational Security, and Data Structuring, enabling end-to-end solutions that drive operational impact.

We are committed to delivering cutting-edge tools and capabilities that address the most complex national security challenges, empowering our partners to stay ahead of emerging threats and ensuring the success of their critical missions. At Clarity, we are people-focused and set on being a destination employer for top talent, offering an environment where innovation thrives, careers grow, and individuals are valued. Join us as we continue to lead innovation and tackle the most pressing challenges in national security.

Position Summary

We are seeking a mid-level engineer with strong cybersecurity leadership skills to join our dynamic team. As a Cyber Security Engineer at Clarity Innovations, you will play a pivotal role in the success of our products.

The candidate must be familiar with DoD network and cyber security standards – guiding the development of Cybersecurity policy, requirements, engineering and certification, and accreditation. The candidate must be familiar with Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements, DISA STIGs. The candidate must understand application of FIPS 140-2 compliance and NIST framework principles, and how these requirements translate to cyber security solutions, processes, configuration implementation, and application requirements.

Primary Responsibilities (included but not limited to):

  • Advises application teams on the security implications of both proposed and actual software modifications, ensuring awareness of risks and the integration of appropriate security measures.
  • Identifies and documents application teams’ proposed and actual changes, and recommended mitigation plans and security measures
  • Conducts comprehensive security engineering analyses, including vulnerability and risk assessments to inform risk decisions and mitigation strategies.
  • Assesses the effectiveness of implemented security controls, ensuring compliance with U.S. Air Force and DoD security standards and objectives.
  • Evaluates applications for potential security risks. Identifies and proposes improvements to security policies, standards and procedures, and risk mitigations / remediation activities.
  • Reviews and analyzes application architectures, data flows, and related processes or documentation to identify security deficiencies, recommending necessary adjustments and validating the implementation of such changes
  • Participates in customer meetings, discussions and decisions. Identifies and proposes improvements to security policies, standards and procedures, and risk mitigation/remediation activities.
  • Supports product development discovery efforts, security architecture design and control evaluation
  • Shares best practices and technical knowledge among multiple teams/portfolios.

Required:

  • Minimum 3 years’ experience with DoD network engineering/management
  • Minimum 3 years specified work in Cyber Security
  • MUST hold at a minimum DoD 8140/8570 certification level: IAT II or IAT III
  • MUST hold at least ONE of the following certifications: CASP+, AWS Security, CCSP, CSSLP (or Associate of ISC2), or equivalent technical security certification or demonstrated experience directly related to the problem domain
  • Specific knowledge that may include, but is not limited to: Unix, DevSecOps, web application security, web application modernization, AWS cloud security, DoD/U.S. Air Force Risk Management Framework and related security policies and practices
  • MUST be eligible to obtain a Common Access Card (CAC)

Non-Technical Competencies:

  • SHALL be comfortable effectively leading a team and setting priorities
  • SHALL be able to provide technical guidance and constructive feedback for development teams to reach compliance
  • Required: Strong communication/general soft skills
  • SHALL conduct themselves at all times in a professional and respectful manner
  • SHALL give and receive feedback in a respectful and professional manner
  • SHALL be a “team player” and contribute to “can-do” culture

Salary Range: $116,000 - $286,000

Pay Range

The posted pay range reflects the anticipated base salary range for this position and is provided to give candidates a general understanding of the compensation opportunity. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the requirements of the position and a variety of job-related factors, which may include geographic location, applicable Federal Government contract labor categories and wage rates, relevant experience, skills and competencies, education, certifications, and the scope and responsibilities of the role.

Because this position may be performed in multiple locations and may be subject to different contract requirements, the salary ultimately offered may vary based on the applicable location and contract. The posted range is not a guarantee of a specific starting salary or an indication that an offer will be made at any particular point within the range.

Total Rewards

In addition to competitive base pay, Clarity provides a Total Rewards package designed to attract and retain exceptional professionals committed to excellence. Our benefits reflect the value we place on skilled individuals who drive our impact in critical digital missions.

At Clarity, a career means joining a high-performing team advancing vital work in the digital landscape. We encourage you to consider the total value of joining us—competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and resources that support your growth and impact.

Our Total Rewards package includes performance-based bonuses, extensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company match, substantial paid time off and holidays, flexible work arrangements where possible, and a range of income protection benefits. We are committed to supporting your well-being, professional growth, and ability to contribute to essential digital missions.

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Salesforce Solutions Architect – Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Salesforce Solutions Architect
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $150,000–$190,000 Annually
Experience Required: 6+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are seeking a Salesforce Solutions Architect to design and govern enterprise Salesforce implementations across Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, and Industry Clouds. The role drives the technical strategy of complex, multi-org Salesforce environments, sets standards for security, integration, and customization, and partners with business stakeholders and engineering teams to deliver scalable, maintainable solutions. The ideal candidate has architected Salesforce at enterprise scale, holds strong opinions on declarative versus programmatic trade-offs, and brings deep platform mastery combined with practical architectural judgment.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Eight or more years of Salesforce experience, with significant time in architecture or technical leadership roles.
  • Deep expertise in Apex, Lightning Web Components, and Flow.
  • Strong understanding of Salesforce data model, sharing model, and platform limits.
  • Hands-on experience with complex Salesforce integrations.
  • Experience designing security models at enterprise scale.
  • Experience with Salesforce DX and modern DevOps tooling.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Salesforce Certified Application Architect or System Architect credentials.
  • Track record of leading large Salesforce programs end-to-end.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Salesforce Certified Technical Architect (CTA) credential.
  • Experience with MuleSoft Anypoint Platform.
  • Familiarity with Industry Clouds such as Financial Services Cloud or Health Cloud.
  • Exposure to Einstein AI / Agentforce features.
  • Experience with multi-org consolidation or M&A integrations.
How to Apply

raw.title: Engineering Project/Process Manager (Prepress Technologies)
raw.excerpt: RRD is seeking an experienced Engineering Project/Process Manager with experience in the print industry!
raw.description:
RRD is seeking an experienced Engineering Project/Process Manager with experience in the print industry!

The ideal candidate will lead, standardize, and innovate our prepress workflows and enterprise color management strategy. In this role, you will be responsible for orchestrating complex technical projects across multiple business units, ensuring seamless technology integration, print standardization, and top-tier color accuracy across all print processes.

He/She should possess deep expertise in prepress automation, workflow management systems (specifically Kodak Prinergy), advanced color science, plate technologies, and vendor management.

Responsibilities

Project Leadership & Workflow Integration

  • Lead end-to-end planning and implementation of technical prepress and color management projects across multiple business units.
  • Manage and orchestrate complex software workflow upgrades, system migrations, and enterprise-wide technology rollouts with minimal disruption to ongoing operations.
  • Develop, maintain, and optimize prepress automation using Kodak Rules-Based Automation (RBA) and Enfocus Switch to drive operational efficiency and error reduction.

Enterprise Color Management & Print Standardization

  • Establish and maintain enterprise-wide color management specifications, standards, and guidelines.
  • Lead print process standardization across digital, proofing, flexographic, and offset printing operations.
  • Perform digital, proofing, and offset press color assessment, and custom color/ICC profile data modeling.
  • Ensure consistent color reproduction across diverse substrates, output devices, and geographical locations.

Prepress & Plate Technologies

  • Oversee and optimize prepress systems centered on the Kodak Prinergy and Esko workflow environment.
  • Maintain working technical knowledge and operational expertise in flexographic and offset plate technologies, imaging devices, and CTP (Computer-to-Plate) output systems.
  • Troubleshoot complex technical prepress and color issues, driving root-cause analysis and corrective actions.

Vendor & Capital Asset Management

  • Manage vendor relationships across multiple touchpoints, including software, hardware, plate materials, and measurement equipment vendors.
  • Lead technical evaluations, specifications, and project delivery for capital equipment and software purchases.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams (Operations, IT, Quality Assurance, and Procurement) to align technical investments with overall business objectives.
  • A Bachelor's degree in Industrial, Process, Mechanical, Engineering or a degree related to Manufacturing Management is preferred.
  • Experience in prepress operations, color management engineering, or graphic communication project management.
  • Minimum of 5 years related experience
  • Project Management: Proven track record of managing complex cross-departmental technical projects, software upgrades, and multi-site implementations
  • Vendor Management: Experience evaluating, negotiating, and managing third-party vendor contracts and capital equipment procurement
  • Ability to execute capital projects by managing groups of employees, equipment manufacturers, and other suppliers both remotely and onsite
  • Manage the estimating, capability analysis and implementation of equipment additions and improvements
  • Develop, utilize and update complex spreadsheets and project management tools to track assets, capabilities, condition, age and replacement plans across the worldwide manufacturing platform.
  • Create detailed models and testing protocols to compare new equipment technologies as they are introduced to facilitate the asset selection process
  • Proven ability to develop relationships by networking within and outside the company to provide rapid responses to manufacturing needs
  • Ability to use Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word is required
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Preferred Industry Specific Skills

  • Workflow Systems: Advanced proficiency with the Kodak Prinergy workflow environment.
  • Automation: Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated workflows using Kodak Rules-Based Automation (RBA) and Enfocus Switch.
  • Color Science: Deep expertise in enterprise color management, color measurement devices, spectral data analysis, ICC profiling, press characterization, raster imaging processing and industry standards (e.g., G7, ISO 12647, FIRST).
  • Print Technology: Strong operational knowledge of flexographic and offset print processes, plate making technologies, and proofing hardware/software.

RRD's current salary range for this role is $99,100 to $158,500 / year. The salary range may be adjusted based on the applicable geographic location of the hired employee, and the range may change in the future. At RRD, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions may vary based upon, but not limited to education, skills, experience, proficiency, performance, shift and location. Depending on the role, in addition to base salary, the total compensation package may also include participation in a bonus, commission or incentive program. RRD’s benefit offerings include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, life insurance and other voluntary supplemental insurance coverages, plus parental leave, adoption assistance, tuition assistance and employer/partner discounts.

RRD is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability/veterans

At RRD, we value innovation, authenticity, and integrity. To uphold the security and fairness of our hiring process, we ask that candidates refrain from using AI tools during interviews to ensure an authentic and secure experience. We appreciate your cooperation as we work to maintain a transparent and equitable hiring process.

All employment offers are contingent upon the successful completion of both a pre-employment background and drug screen.

RRD provides marketing, packaging, print, and business services to the world’s most respected brands. The company’s proprietary technology, advanced data analytics, and expertise fuel organizational decision-making from strategy through execution, delivering sustainable solutions with the lowest possible environmental impact. Global organizations and regulated industries trust RRD to reduce complexity and drive audience connections across the entire customer journey.
